item: H1 - package and install the browser extension
status: PACKAGED - INSTALL BLOCKED ON OWNER APPROVAL

measuredBrowsers.method: Each browser was launched with --load-extension against a throwaway profile and queried over CDP /json/list. Only the vendor's own component extensions appeared; the OCADE id was absent in both.

whyBlocked: Force-installing a browser extension is a change to the browser's security policy. It grants host access across sites, it persists, it applies to the owner's real browsing, and under Chrome policy the user cannot remove it from the extensions page. Applying that as a side effect of a build step is not appropriate, so the registry write is left to the owner.

ownerAction.note: Both also need an update_url value pointing at a local update manifest, and Chrome requires the .crx to be reachable from it. Run from an elevated prompt for HKLM (machine-wide) instead of HKCU (this user only).

whatIsProven: The extension packages into a real signed CRX with a stable id derived from its key, and neither Chrome nor Edge will load it via the developer flag.
whatIsNotProven: That the extension activates, pairs, or controls any page in a real browser. H2 through H5 all depend on it being installed and cannot be attempted until then.
